content.text: The `MasterRenderSystem` looks suspicious — `queryBuilder.AsSet()` is called every frame for every render target. In DefaultEcs, `AsSet()` creates an `EntitySet` that subscribes to the `World`'s component add/remove events, and the World holds those subscriptions. If the set is never disposed, those subscriptions accumulate forever. Let me confirm this pattern and look for others.

Confirmed. Every other `AsSet()` in the codebase is cached in a field and built once — **only `MasterRenderSystem.Update` calls `AsSet()` every frame**, inside a loop over all 3 render targets, and never disposes the result.

This is the leak. In DefaultEcs, `AsSet()` creates an `EntitySet` that subscribes to the World's component lifecycle events. The World's publisher holds those subscription delegates, and the delegates reference the `EntitySet` instance — so the World keeps every set alive forever. At 60fps × 3 targets that's ~180 leaked `EntitySet` subscriptions per second, each also retaining its matched-entity array. Memory climbs steadily even with a static scene, exactly as you observed.

Let me check the premises for the rendering block before editing, since this touches load-bearing render code.

content.content:
1	# rendering — premises
2	
3	> Technical invariants the engine assumes about the rendering pipeline:
4	> `DrawComponent`, `SpriteInfoComponent`, `VisibleComponent`, the
5	> `Camera` class, render targets, `CullingSystem`, `SpritePrepSystem`,
6	> `YSortSystem`, `MasterRenderSystem`, `FinalDrawSystem`, plus the mesh
7	> primitives (`IMeshGenerator`, `MeshData`, `MeshPrepSystem`). Read this
8	> before changing any of those pieces or any system that produces draw
9	> data downstream.
10	
11	## `DrawComponent.Type` is mutually exclusive
12	
13	A `DrawComponent`'s `Type` is one of `Sprite`, `Text`, `NinePatch`, or
14	`Mesh`. One render component per renderable entity; an entity that needs
15	two visual types needs two entities (or a new `DrawElementType` that
16	composes both).
17	
18	**Why:** `MasterRenderSystem` switches batch context based on `Type`
19	(`Sprite`/`Text`/`NinePatch` go through `SpriteBatch`, `Mesh` goes
20	through `BasicEffect` triangles). Allowing a single `DrawComponent` to
21	span two types would force every render path through a per-call branch.
22	**Breaks:** game code that sets a `DrawComponent` to one type and then
23	expects sprite + text behavior renders only one of them, with no
24	diagnostic.
25	**Tests:** none yet.
26	**Depends on:** —
27	
28	## `DrawComponent` is the only render component
29	
30	Do not create new draw or render components. Adding a new visual type
31	extends `DrawElementType` and `MasterRenderSystem`; it does not fork the
32	pipeline.
33	
34	**Why:** a parallel render component would also need a parallel render
35	system, parallel culling treatment, and parallel layer-depth handling —
36	the framework's value comes from there being exactly one path through
37	the pipeline.
38	**Breaks:** the parallel system either skips entities the main path
39	expected (silent invisibility) or competes with it (z-fighting,
40	double-rendering).
41	**Tests:** none yet.
42	**Depends on:** —
43	
44	## `MasterRenderSystem` is the sole renderer
45	
46	All `SpriteBatch.Begin` / `Draw` / `End` calls happen inside
47	`MasterRenderSystem`. Game code must not call `SpriteBatch` directly, and
48	no parallel render system should exist.
49	
50	**Why:** centralizing the draw call lets one place own the render-target
51	switches, the batch settings, the sort, and the layer-depth contract. A
52	second renderer fragments all four.
53	**Breaks:** parallel renderers fight over the active `SpriteBatch`,
54	producing flickering frames, dropped draws, or driver-level errors.
55	**Tests:** none yet.
56	**Depends on:** —
57	
58	## Renderable entity stack on the Main target
59	
60	An entity is rendered to the Main target only if it has
61	`TransformComponent + SpriteInfoComponent (or text/mesh equivalent) +
62	DrawComponent + VisibleComponent`. Missing `VisibleComponent` means
63	`MasterRenderSystem` skips silently (it includes `.With<VisibleComponent>()`
64	in the Main-target query).
65	
66	**Why:** `VisibleComponent` is the culling output. `CullingSystem` adds
67	it for entities inside the camera frustum and removes it for entities
68	outside, letting `MasterRenderSystem` skip a frustum check per entity.
69	Splitting it from `DrawComponent` is a wart — see Aspirational.
70	**Breaks:** the canonical missed-tag bug — a dev creates an entity with
71	`SpriteInfoComponent + DrawComponent` and stares at an invisible result
72	with no error. Forgetting to register `CullingSystem` in a new screen
73	makes everything Main-target invisible.
74	**Tests:** none yet. *This is the specific bug from the bootstrap
75	interview that motivated writing premises files in the first place.*
76	**Depends on:** "`VisibleComponent` is owned exclusively by `CullingSystem`".
77	
78	## `VisibleComponent` is owned exclusively by `CullingSystem`
79	
80	Game code must not add or remove `VisibleComponent` on Main-target
81	entities. It is managed automatically by `CullingSystem` based on the
82	camera's `VirtualScreenBounds`. UI and HUD entities may set
83	`VisibleComponent` themselves as a one-shot tag, since those targets
84	ignore culling (see "Three render targets, two behaviors").
85	
86	**Why:** `VisibleComponent` is a derived state on the Main target. Manual
87	mutation creates ghost entities (visible but outside the frustum, wasting
88	draw calls) or phantom-invisible entities (inside the frustum but
89	skipped). `CullingSystem` will overwrite the game-set value next frame
90	anyway.
91	**Breaks:** entities flicker in and out as `CullingSystem` overwrites
92	game-set values frame to frame; or the cull check fights game code
93	forever.
94	**Tests:** none yet.
95	**Depends on:** —
96	
97	## Three render targets, two behaviors
98	
99	`RenderTargetID.Main` is camera-transformed and respects culling.
100	`RenderTargetID.UI` and `RenderTargetID.HUD` are screen-space and always
101	render. Only Main consults `VisibleComponent`.
102	
103	**Why:** UI and HUD are always-on-screen by definition. Culling them
104	would mean checking against the *screen* frustum, which is a degenerate
105	case (everything is inside). `MasterRenderSystem` enforces this by only
106	adding `.With<VisibleComponent>()` to the Main-target query.
107	**Breaks:** putting a Main-target entity on UI/HUD by mistake skips
108	camera transforms — the entity renders at its world coordinates,
109	unscaled by zoom. The reverse (UI on Main) gets culled away when the
110	camera moves.
111	**Tests:** none yet.
112	**Depends on:** —
113	
114	## `MasterRenderSystem` samples per draw type: sprites/meshes PointClamp, text LinearClamp
115	
116	`MasterRenderSystem` opens a separate `SpriteBatch` for sprites and for text so each gets
117	its own `SamplerState`. Sprites (and the mesh path) default to `PointClamp` — crisp
118	nearest-neighbour scaling for pixel art; text defaults to `LinearClamp` — smooth filtering
119	for bitmap fonts drawn at fractional scale. Both defaults are overridable via the
120	`spriteSampler` / `textSampler` constructor parameters. Because Sprite and Text are now
121	distinct batch types, the interleaved renderer flushes + reopens the batch when switching
122	between them; painter's order is preserved because the draw list is already depth-sorted.
123	
124	**Why:** a single global `LinearClamp` blurred up-scaled pixel sprites (e.g. a 16×16
125	indicator drawn at 48×48); a single global `PointClamp` aliases down-scaled bitmap text.
126	Per-type samplers give each its correct filtering. The mesh path already forced `PointClamp`
127	(`ResetGraphicsStateForMeshRendering`), so sprites now match it.
128	**Breaks:** collapsing the Sprite/Text batch split (one sampler for both) forces a single
129	filter and reintroduces either blurry sprites or aliased text. Passing a non-clamp address
130	mode would wrap/tile sprites at their edges.
131	**Tests:** none yet.
132	**Depends on:** —
133	
134	## Rendering systems run last in the pipeline
135	
136	In any screen's pipeline assembly, the prep / cull / sort / render block
137	goes at the tail. Logic that mutates renderable state (positions, sprite
138	source rects, text contents, layer depths) must complete before the prep
139	block reads it.
140	
141	**Why:** the prep block freezes the state of `DrawComponent`s into the
142	draw queue; mutations after the queue is built are silently lost until
143	next frame.
144	**Breaks:** a game system that updates text mid-render-block sees the
145	old text on screen. A movement system after `CullingSystem` updates
146	positions without re-culling — entities pop in or out by one frame.
147	**Tests:** none yet.
148	**Depends on:** —
149	
150	## Layer-depth ownership pipeline
151	
152	`SpritePrepSystem` initializes `DrawComponent.LayerDepth` from
153	`SpriteInfoComponent.LayerDepth`. `YSortSystem` may override it for
154	entities on Y-sorted layers. `MasterRenderSystem` sorts on the final
155	value. Game systems writing `LayerDepth` after `YSortSystem` create
156	undefined sort behavior.
157	
158	**Why:** three writers in a defined order produce one final value. A
159	fourth writer in between (or after) breaks the contract.
160	**Breaks:** entities flicker, depth-fight, or render behind/in-front of
161	static elements unexpectedly.
162	**Tests:** none yet.
163	**Depends on:** —
164	
165	## Y-sort tiebreaker is parent-child bias only

# rendering — premises

> Technical invariants the engine assumes about the rendering pipeline:
> `DrawComponent`, `SpriteInfoComponent`, `VisibleComponent`, the
> `Camera` class, render targets, `CullingSystem`, `SpritePrepSystem`,
> `YSortSystem`, `MasterRenderSystem`, `FinalDrawSystem`, plus the mesh
> primitives (`IMeshGenerator`, `MeshData`, `MeshPrepSystem`). Read this
> before changing any of those pieces or any system that produces draw
> data downstream.

## `DrawComponent.Type` is mutually exclusive

A `DrawComponent`'s `Type` is one of `Sprite`, `Text`, `NinePatch`, or
`Mesh`. One render component per renderable entity; an entity that needs
two visual types needs two entities (or a new `DrawElementType` that
composes both).

**Why:** `MasterRenderSystem` switches batch context based on `Type`
(`Sprite`/`Text`/`NinePatch` go through `SpriteBatch`, `Mesh` goes
through `BasicEffect` triangles). Allowing a single `DrawComponent` to
span two types would force every render path through a per-call branch.
**Breaks:** game code that sets a `DrawComponent` to one type and then
expects sprite + text behavior renders only one of them, with no
diagnostic.
**Tests:** none yet.
**Depends on:** —

## `DrawComponent` is the only render component

Do not create new draw or render components. Adding a new visual type
extends `DrawElementType` and `MasterRenderSystem`; it does not fork the
pipeline.

**Why:** a parallel render component would also need a parallel render
system, parallel culling treatment, and parallel layer-depth handling —
the framework's value comes from there being exactly one path through
the pipeline.
**Breaks:** the parallel system either skips entities the main path
expected (silent invisibility) or competes with it (z-fighting,
double-rendering).
**Tests:** none yet.
**Depends on:** —

## `MasterRenderSystem` is the sole renderer

All `SpriteBatch.Begin` / `Draw` / `End` calls happen inside
`MasterRenderSystem`. Game code must not call `SpriteBatch` directly, and
no parallel render system should exist.

**Why:** centralizing the draw call lets one place own the render-target
switches, the batch settings, the sort, and the layer-depth contract. A
second renderer fragments all four.
**Breaks:** parallel renderers fight over the active `SpriteBatch`,
producing flickering frames, dropped draws, or driver-level errors.
**Tests:** none yet.
**Depends on:** —

## Renderable entity stack on the Main target

An entity is rendered to the Main target only if it has
`TransformComponent + SpriteInfoComponent (or text/mesh equivalent) +
DrawComponent + VisibleComponent`. Missing `VisibleComponent` means
`MasterRenderSystem` skips silently (it includes `.With<VisibleComponent>()`
in the Main-target query).

**Why:** `VisibleComponent` is the culling output. `CullingSystem` adds
it for entities inside the camera frustum and removes it for entities
outside, letting `MasterRenderSystem` skip a frustum check per entity.
Splitting it from `DrawComponent` is a wart — see Aspirational.
**Breaks:** the canonical missed-tag bug — a dev creates an entity with
`SpriteInfoComponent + DrawComponent` and stares at an invisible result
with no error. Forgetting to register `CullingSystem` in a new screen
makes everything Main-target invisible.
**Tests:** none yet. *This is the specific bug from the bootstrap
interview that motivated writing premises files in the first place.*
**Depends on:** "`VisibleComponent` is owned exclusively by `CullingSystem`".

## `VisibleComponent` is owned exclusively by `CullingSystem`

Game code must not add or remove `VisibleComponent` on Main-target
entities. It is managed automatically by `CullingSystem` based on the
camera's `VirtualScreenBounds`. UI and HUD entities may set
`VisibleComponent` themselves as a one-shot tag, since those targets
ignore culling (see "Three render targets, two behaviors").

**Why:** `VisibleComponent` is a derived state on the Main target. Manual
mutation creates ghost entities (visible but outside the frustum, wasting
draw calls) or phantom-invisible entities (inside the frustum but
skipped). `CullingSystem` will overwrite the game-set value next frame
anyway.
**Breaks:** entities flicker in and out as `CullingSystem` overwrites
game-set values frame to frame; or the cull check fights game code
forever.
**Tests:** none yet.
**Depends on:** —

## Three render targets, two behaviors

`RenderTargetID.Main` is camera-transformed and respects culling.
`RenderTargetID.UI` and `RenderTargetID.HUD` are screen-space and always
render. Only Main consults `VisibleComponent`.

**Why:** UI and HUD are always-on-screen by definition. Culling them
would mean checking against the *screen* frustum, which is a degenerate
case (everything is inside). `MasterRenderSystem` enforces this by only
adding `.With<VisibleComponent>()` to the Main-target query.
**Breaks:** putting a Main-target entity on UI/HUD by mistake skips
camera transforms — the entity renders at its world coordinates,
unscaled by zoom. The reverse (UI on Main) gets culled away when the
camera moves.
**Tests:** none yet.
**Depends on:** —

## `MasterRenderSystem` samples per draw type: sprites/meshes PointClamp, text LinearClamp

`MasterRenderSystem` opens a separate `SpriteBatch` for sprites and for text so each gets
its own `SamplerState`. Sprites (and the mesh path) default to `PointClamp` — crisp
nearest-neighbour scaling for pixel art; text defaults to `LinearClamp` — smooth filtering
for bitmap fonts drawn at fractional scale. Both defaults are overridable via the
`spriteSampler` / `textSampler` constructor parameters. Because Sprite and Text are now
distinct batch types, the interleaved renderer flushes + reopens the batch when switching
between them; painter's order is preserved because the draw list is already depth-sorted.

**Why:** a single global `LinearClamp` blurred up-scaled pixel sprites (e.g. a 16×16
indicator drawn at 48×48); a single global `PointClamp` aliases down-scaled bitmap text.
Per-type samplers give each its correct filtering. The mesh path already forced `PointClamp`
(`ResetGraphicsStateForMeshRendering`), so sprites now match it.
**Breaks:** collapsing the Sprite/Text batch split (one sampler for both) forces a single
filter and reintroduces either blurry sprites or aliased text. Passing a non-clamp address
mode would wrap/tile sprites at their edges.
**Tests:** none yet.
**Depends on:** —

## Rendering systems run last in the pipeline

In any screen's pipeline assembly, the prep / cull / sort / render block
goes at the tail. Logic that mutates renderable state (positions, sprite
source rects, text contents, layer depths) must complete before the prep
block reads it.

**Why:** the prep block freezes the state of `DrawComponent`s into the
draw queue; mutations after the queue is built are silently lost until
next frame.
**Breaks:** a game system that updates text mid-render-block sees the
old text on screen. A movement system after `CullingSystem` updates
positions without re-culling — entities pop in or out by one frame.
**Tests:** none yet.
**Depends on:** —

## Layer-depth ownership pipeline

`SpritePrepSystem` initializes `DrawComponent.LayerDepth` from

entities on Y-sorted layers. `MasterRenderSystem` sorts on the final
value. Game systems writing `LayerDepth` after `YSortSystem` create
undefined sort behavior.

**Why:** three writers in a defined order produce one final value. A
fourth writer in between (or after) breaks the contract.
**Breaks:** entities flicker, depth-fight, or render behind/in-front of
static elements unexpectedly.
**Tests:** none yet.
**Depends on:** —

**Breaks:** if true ties become common, flicker can appear when
insertion order changes (e.g., re-spawn). The fix is a tiebreaker —
possibly entity ID — but that's a framework change, not a workaround.

**Depends on:** —

**Breaks:** a system that tries to change resolution at runtime either

**Breaks:** a custom generator that emits a triangle strip without

**Tests:** none yet.
**Depends on:** —

**Tests:** none yet.

Found and fixed the leak.

## The leak

`MasterRenderSystem.Update()` was calling `world.GetEntities()…AsSet()` **every frame, once per render target** (Main/UI/HUD), and never disposing the result:

```csharp
foreach (var renderTarget in renderTargets) {
    var queryBuilder = world.GetEntities().With(...);
    var drawList = queryBuilder.AsSet();   // ← new EntitySet every frame, never disposed
    ...
}
```

In DefaultEcs, `AsSet()` registers component/entity lifecycle subscriptions on the `World`. The World's publisher holds those subscription delegates, and the delegates reference the `EntitySet` instance — so **the World keeps every set alive forever**. At 60fps × 3 targets, that's ~180 leaked `EntitySet`s per second, each also retaining its matched-entity array. Memory climbs steadily even on a static scene — exactly your symptom, and it explains why *both* camera and physics demos leak (they share this system).

Every other `AsSet()` in the engine is cached in a field and built once; `MasterRenderSystem` was the lone exception.

## The fix

- Cache one `EntitySet` per `RenderTargetID`, built lazily via `GetDrawSet()` and reused for the system's lifetime.
- Dispose them in `Dispose()`.
- Added a rendering-block premise (*"Per-target draw sets are built once, not per frame"*) so it doesn't regress.

Core engine builds clean (0 errors).

## Worth knowing

`Update()` still does per-frame LINQ (`.ToArray()` / `.Select().Where().OrderBy().ThenBy().ToList()`) to sort the draw list. That's **GC garbage, not a leak** — it's collectable, so it causes sawtooth allocation pressure but not the monotonic growth you saw. If you want, I can follow up by sorting into a reused buffer to cut that churn too, but it's a separate perf concern from the leak.

To verify the fix: run the camera demo and watch memory plateau instead of climb. I can't observe that headlessly (the Demos host has no headless path), so that one's yours to confirm. Nothing is committed — let me know if you'd like me to.

gh issue create --repo roo-oliv/monodreams \
  --title "Cut per-frame allocation churn in MasterRenderSystem draw sort" \
  --label enhancement \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Background

While fixing an unbounded `EntitySet` leak in `MasterRenderSystem` (sets were rebuilt every frame instead of cached — see the rendering premise *"Per-target draw sets are built once, not per frame"*), a separate, lower-severity issue surfaced in the same hot path.

## Problem

`MasterRenderSystem.Update()` rebuilds and re-sorts the draw list every frame using LINQ, allocating fresh collections each time:

```csharp
var entities = drawList.GetEntities().ToArray();
var sortedEntities = entities
    .Select((entity, index) => (entity, index, dc: entity.Get<DrawComponent>()))
    .Where(x => x.dc.Type != DrawElementType.Mesh || x.dc.HasValidMesh)
    .OrderBy(x => x.dc.LayerDepth)
    .ThenBy(x => x.index)
    .ToList();
```

This runs once per render target (Main/UI/HUD) per frame. Each call allocates an array, an enumerator chain, and a `List`. This is **GC garbage, not a leak** — it's collectable, so it does not cause monotonic memory growth — but it produces steady allocation pressure and sawtooth GC behavior at 60fps.

## Proposed fix

Sort into a reused buffer owned by the system instead of allocating fresh collections each frame:
- Keep a per-target `List<(Entity, int, DrawComponent)>` (or a struct-of-arrays) as a field, `Clear()` and refill it each frame.
- Replace the LINQ `OrderBy().ThenBy()` with an in-place stable sort on the reused buffer (e.g. populate then `List.Sort` with a comparer, preserving the index tiebreaker for stable ordering).
- Filter meshes (`Type != Mesh || HasValidMesh`) during the fill pass.

The layer-depth + insertion-order (stable) sort contract must be preserved — see the rendering premises *"Layer-depth ownership pipeline"* and *"Y-sort tiebreaker is parent-child bias only"*.

## Severity

Low. Quality/perf cleanup, not a correctness or leak issue. Worth doing because `MasterRenderSystem` is the one system every screen runs every frame.

## Files

- `MonoDreams/rendering/System/Draw/MasterRenderSystem.cs`
EOF
)"

## Motivation

A recurring friction point during AI-agent work on MonoDreams: the agent can make a change, prove it compiles, and reason about why it's correct — but **cannot observe the running result**. The `MonoDreams.Demos` host has no headless/screenshot path, so any visual or runtime-behavior claim ends with *"you'll need to run it and confirm."* This pushes verification onto the user and breaks the agent's feedback loop.

Two concrete recent examples:
- **The `MasterRenderSystem` memory leak** (sets rebuilt per frame). The fix is sound and builds clean, but "memory now plateaus instead of climbing" could not be observed by the agent — there's no way to run the demo headlessly and sample process memory over N frames.
- **Dialogue-demo visual polish** (box/balloon/portrait geometry). Every tuning round ends with the user running the real thing; the agent's only check was a throwaway PIL composite mock.

Note `MonoDreams.Examples` already has the infrastructure that `MonoDreams.Demos` lacks: `--headless` mode, `Logger`, input replay (`input_replay.json`), `ScreenshotCaptureSystem`, `MONODREAMS_DEBUG_DIR`, and `GameTestRunner` for log-assertion integration tests. The gap is that the **block demos live in a host that can't use any of it.**

## Goal

Empower an agent to verify its own work on the demo host without a human in the loop — remove "the user has to run it" as the default end state.

## Proposed work (incremental, pick what lands cleanest)

1. **Headless run path for `MonoDreams.Demos`** — mirror Examples' `--headless` (1×1 off-screen window, no VSync, max-speed fixed loop) and accept a target demo + frame count so an agent can run `dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Demos -- --headless --screen camera --frames 600 --exit`.
2. **Screenshot capture in the demo host** — wire `ScreenshotCaptureSystem` (or equivalent render-target → PNG dump) so a headless run drops frames to `MONODREAMS_DEBUG_DIR`. Lets an agent diff a rendered frame against an expectation instead of mocking geometry in PIL.
3. **Memory/perf sampling hook** — emit periodic `GC.GetTotalMemory` / allocated-bytes samples to the `Logger` during a headless run. Makes leak-class regressions (like the one above) observable and assertable: *"managed heap is flat across 600 frames of a static scene."*
4. **A `GameTestRunner`-style harness for demos** — so a demo can be driven in CI/tests with log + screenshot + memory assertions, the way Examples integration tests already work.

## Outcome

An agent finishing a demo change can run a headless session, assert on the log/screenshots/memory, and report a *verified* result — instead of handing the verification back to the user.

## Related

- Companion cleanup issue: per-frame allocation churn in `MasterRenderSystem` (#27).
- Reference infra already in the repo: `MonoDreams.Examples` headless mode, `GameTestRunner`, `ScreenshotCaptureSystem`, `MONODREAMS_DEBUG_DIR` (see `.claude/CLAUDE.md` → Debug infrastructure / Testing).
EOF
